title: Site-specific fluorescence double-labeling of proteins and analysis of structural changes in solution by Fluorescence Resonance Energy Transfer (FRET)
author: Patel, Yilmaz, et al.
materials: All buffers and solutions used in this study were prepared using ACS reagent grade chemicals from Fischer Scientific (Pittsburgh, PA). The modified oligonucleotides used to construct the wild-type DnaABA (DnaAwt) and DnaA1 mutant by PCR amplification and in vitro mutagenesis, were synthesized by Sigma-Genosys Corp. (Woodlands, TX). The procedure for cloning the DnaABA from Bacillus anthracis (Stern strain) has been discussed previously [6]. We chose Alexa568 maleimide (Life Technologies, Grand Island, NY) to label a single cysteine in the protein as an acceptor fluorophore and FlAsH-EDT2 (Life Technologies, Grand Island, NY) to label the specific CCPGCC sequence.

The purified DnaAwt and DnaA1 mutant were stored in a buffer consisting of 10% glycerol, 20 mM Hepes (pH 7.5), 1 mM EDTA (pH 8.0), 5 mM MgCl2, 0.01% NP40 and 0.5 mM TCEP and frozen in −80 °C until labeling. The buffer used for protein recovery after labeling contained 10% glycerol, 20 mM Hepes (pH 7.5), 5 mM MgCl2, 0.01% NP40 and 0.5 mM TCEP. Proteins were added to anisotropy buffer, containing 20 mM Hepes (pH 7.4), 5% (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM EDTA (pH 8.0), 5 mM MgCl2, 0.1 mM TCEP and 0.1 mg/ml BSA.

The FlAsH and Alexa568 maleimide fluorophores work best in physiological conditions with a close to neutral pH of 7.5. Fluorescence labeling procedures were carried out in dark and using black polypropylene Eppendorf tubes (Thermo Scientific, Pittsburgh, PA). Purified recombinant protein (200 μg) was incubated at 16 °C overnight with 3 molar excess of FlAsH-EDT2 to crosslink with the C-terminus CCPGCC sequence (Fig. 1B). For overnight incubation of recombinant protein with FlAsH fluorophore, we used a PCR apparatus for controlled parameters of 16 °C for 12 h and then 4 °C until removed from PCR. Labeling the CCPGCC sequence with molar excess of FlAsH fluorophore first was done to avoid nonspecific labeling of Alexa568 maleimide to the four cysteines. FlAsH covalently attaches with all four Cys sulfhydryl groups in the Cys4 sequence at the C-terminus. Alexa568 maleimide (1.1 equivalent) was then added to the FlAsH-labeled protein at 4 °C and incubated for 10 min in a dark setting for single Cys labeling (Fig. 1C).

The double-labeled protein was immediately purified from unincorporated fluorophores using a 40 K, 0.5 ml Zeba desalting spin column (Thermo Scientific, Pittsburgh, PA) with labeling buffer as eluant. EDTA, mercaptoethanol, and DTT must be avoided as these have the potential to chelate the arsenics or quench FlAsH. For optimal labeling, the protein must be in the reduced form to avoid disulfide bridge formation and to allow fluorophore to cysteine-SH coupling reaction. TCEP (0.1 mM), with no free sulfhydryl group, was found to be a suitable reducing agent for site-specific labeling of proteins. Following the protocol, provided by the manufacturer, labeling buffer with TCEP was used to equilibrate the resin prior to using the spin-column to purify fluorophore-labeled proteins. The spin column was centrifuged at 1500 × g for two minutes on a bench-top microcentrifuge in a dark room. The purified double-labeled protein was aliquoted and stored in the same buffer at −80 °C. In addition, the spin column purification needed to be optimized for each protein before proceeding with fluorescence spectroscopy.

steps.title: Prepare all required buffers
steps.instruction: Make three buffers using ACS‑grade reagents: (1) Storage buffer – 10 % glycerol, 20 mM Hepes pH 7.5, 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.01 % NP40, 0.5 mM TCEP; aliquot and freeze at –80 °C. (2) Recovery buffer – 10 % glycerol, 20 mM Hepes pH 7.5, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.01 % NP40, 0.5 mM TCEP. (3) Anisotropy buffer – 20 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 5 % (v/v) glycerol, 1 mM EDTA pH 8.0, 5 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 mM TCEP, 0.1 mg ml⁻¹ BSA.

steps.title: Construct DnaA wild‑type and mutant plasmids
steps.instruction: Amplify DnaA_BA (B. anthracis) by PCR with Q5 polymerase using the following primers: forward 5′‑TCTTCTCATATGGAAACATCTGTGATTTATGG‑3′, reverse 5′‑CTCCTCCTCGAGTCATTACTAGCCGCCACCGCAACAGCCAGGACAACACTTTAAAATATCGTTAATTTC‑3′ to generate DnaA_wt (S5C + C‑terminal CCPGCCGG). For DnaA1 (C83S + CCPGCCGGG) first PCR with forward 5′‑TCTTCTCATATGGAAAACATCTCTGATTTATGG‑3′, same reverse, then perform Quik‑Change Lightning mutagenesis (S83C). Verify plasmids by bidirectional sequencing before expression.

steps.title: Label protein with FlAsH‑EDT2
steps.instruction: Thaw purified DnaA_wt or DnaA1 (stored in storage buffer) and adjust concentration to 200 µg protein per labeling reaction. In a black polypropylene Eppendorf tube, add 3‑fold molar excess of FlAsH‑EDT2 relative to the C‑terminal CCPGCC motif. Incubate at 16 °C for 12 h in a PCR thermocycler, then keep at 4 °C until the next step. Perform all steps in the dark.

steps.title: Label protein with Alexa568 maleimide
steps.instruction: After FlAsH labeling, add Alexa568 maleimide at 1.1 equivalent (relative to the single surface Cys) to the same reaction mixture kept at 4 °C. Incubate for 10 min in the dark to label the engineered cysteine (S5C or S83C).

steps.title: Purify double‑labeled protein
steps.instruction: Equilibrate a 40 kDa, 0.5 ml Zeba desalting spin column with labeling buffer containing 0.1 mM TCEP (avoid EDTA, mercaptoethanol, DTT). Load the FlAsH‑ then Alexa568‑labeled protein onto the column and centrifuge at 1500 × g for 2 min in a dark room. Collect the flow‑through (protein) and immediately aliquot; store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Determine protein and fluorophore concentrations
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration by Bradford assay and by Nanodrop 3000 (A₂₈₀). Measure fluorophore concentrations spectrophotometrically: FlAsH absorbance at 528 nm (ε = 70 000 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹) and Alexa568 at 578 nm (ε = 91 300 M⁻¹ cm⁻¹). Verify that donor‑to‑acceptor ratios are ≈1:1 (0.95–1.05) for double‑labeled samples; for single‑labeled FlAsH samples the FlAsH:protein ratio should be 1.0 ± 0.6.

steps.title: Prepare fluorescence measurement samples
steps.instruction: Add 0.2 µg of double‑labeled DnaA (final 4 nM) to 1 ml anisotropy buffer in a standard quartz cuvette. For substrate‑dependent measurements, pre‑incubate protein with 500 µM ATP or ADP and/or 100 nM specific dsDNA for 2 min at 30 °C before placing in the cuvette. Keep all samples in the dark until measurement.

steps.title: Acquire steady‑state fluorescence spectra
steps.instruction: Set the photon‑counting spectrofluorometer to 25 °C (dark room). Use excitation wavelength 500 nm, slit width 5 nm, integration time 1 nm s⁻¹, and record emission from 500 nm to 650 nm. First record a blank with anisotropy buffer alone. Then record each protein sample as three consecutive scans; the instrument automatically averages each set. Repeat the entire three‑scan acquisition three times (total 9 scans) for each condition.

steps.title: Normalize raw spectra
steps.instruction: Export wavelength and intensity data to Microsoft Excel, then import into the free Fluortools “a/e‑UV‑vis‑IR Spectral Software”. Choose a normalization wavelength (e.g., the donor peak maximum) and apply the equation: normalized intensity = (intensity at each wavelength / intensity at chosen wavelength) × multiplication factor. Determine the multiplication factor empirically to obtain a well‑scaled spectrum. Save the normalized data.

steps.title: Plot normalized spectra
steps.instruction: Open GraphPad Prism 5.0, import the normalized data, and create a line graph with wavelength (510–650 nm) on the x‑axis and fluorescence intensity on the y‑axis. Apply the built‑in smoothing function for visual clarity. Export graphs for further analysis.

steps.title: Deconvolute donor and acceptor peaks
steps.instruction: In Fluortools, select the Gaussian‑band tool. For the FlAsH emission peak, define the left and right boundaries and fit a Gaussian curve. Repeat the procedure for the Alexa568 emission peak. Record the Gaussian‑fitted peak intensities (ID for donor, IA for acceptor).

steps.title: Calculate FRET parameters
steps.instruction: Using the Gaussian‑derived intensities, compute: (1) Proximity ratio P = IA / (IA + ID). (2) FRET efficiency EFRET = 1 – (FDA / FD), where FD is the donor‑only intensity and FDA is the donor intensity in the presence of acceptor. (3) Inter‑fluorophore distance r = R₀ × [(1 – EFRET)/EFRET]¹⁄⁶, with R₀ = 75 Å for the FlAsH‑Alexa568 pair. Perform the calculations in a prepared Excel sheet containing the formulas.
